owned-cpp-callback-results:
    name: Callback-result lifetimes in installed C++ packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 150
    env:
      EMCC_CORES: "2"
    steps:
      - name: Check out the exact revision
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
      - name: Install callback acceptance tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake git jq libgmp-dev libuv1-dev m4 pkg-config python3 ripgrep zstd
          npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          bash scripts/bootstrap-toolchains.sh
      - name: Install all callback browser engines
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit
      - name: Build the callback shared runtime
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p build
          bash scripts/build-lean-link-spike.sh 2>&1 | tee build/owned-cpp-callback-result-runtime.log
          test -s build/lean-link-spike/lazy/main.wasm
      - name: Verify C++ callback-result lifetimes
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/env.sh
          npm run test:owned-cpp-callback-results 2>&1 | tee build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
          rg '^# tests 12$' build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
          rg '^# pass 12$' build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
          rg '^# fail 0$' build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
          rg '^# cancelled 0$' build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
          rg '^# skipped 0$' build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/ordinary-base-nohost.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/ordinary-base-host.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/ordinary-combined.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/ordinary-no-host-package.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/ordinary-combined-package.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/ordinary-combined-release.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/reviewed-base-nohost.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/reviewed-base-host.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/reviewed-combined.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/reviewed-no-host-package.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/reviewed-combined-package.json
          test -s build/owned-cpp-callback-results/reviewed-combined-release.json
      - name: Preserve C++ callback-result acceptance
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: cpp-callback-results-${{ github.sha }}
          path: |
            build/owned-cpp-callback-results/
            build/owned-cpp-callback-results.log
            build/owned-cpp-callback-result-runtime.log
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

- name: Enforce C++ callback-result acceptance
        if: needs.owned-cpp-callback-results.result != 'success'
        run: exit 1

## C++ callback-result lifetimes

Run the C++ gate with the same native, Emscripten and browser dependencies:

```sh
npm run test:owned-cpp-callback-results
```

The gate requires 12 passing tests with no skips and 12 JSON reports in
`build/owned-cpp-callback-results/`. Both authoring paths compile normal and
sanitized consumers, inject allocation failures before and after ownership
transfer, and reject deliberately broken lifetime implementations.

Installed checks cover explicit callback-disabled native builds and combined
callback, receiver, result-anchor and transfer packages built by the installed
CLI. Consumers use pkg-config and relocated CMake after producer removal.
Independent builds and reassembly must reproduce the original archives. Separate
C/C++/npm releases exercise all three projections, browser contexts and the
published C++ and JavaScript examples. CI requires every report and propagates
the C++ job's failure through the consumer summary.
For C, C++ and npm, a nested [`callable.result` contract](../publish/c.md#anchor-a-callback-result-to-its-argument)

### Anchor a callback result to its argument

Use the nested [callback-result contract](c.md#anchor-a-callback-result-to-its-argument)
to select a callback-local argument as the result's lifetime anchor. Ordinary
configuration uses `arg0`, `arg1`, and so on. Reviewed contracts use their own
callback parameter names. Neither the outer export's arguments nor the closure
handle count toward those positions.

Build with `--target cpp`. Returned closure calls require the selected argument
as `Value<T>` and return a checked `Value<Result>`. Host callback replies accept
the declared value or its whole-owner wrapper. See the
[consumer example](../consume/cpp.md#callback-result-owners).

These contracts use native model version 11, native component receipt version 7,
package manifest version 7, `ownedValues` version 6 and `cppValues` version 5.
Packaging regenerates the selected argument, expiry, retention and host-reply
rules from compiler metadata and verifies the generated source. Callback-local
anchors work without ordinary result anchors, methods, or host callbacks.
Packages without callback-result anchors keep their existing contract versions.
